status: researched, not routed — no tour from this file ships yet
note: Step 1 and step 2 of the pipeline for a Bergen round: candidates with a published ski-touring description, and every summit resolved against the place-name register and Kartverket's 1 m terrain model. Corridors, routing, measurement and the guides are still to do. Nothing here has been routed, so nothing here is in lib/tours.ts.
why: Bergen is the largest hole in the map. The nearest tour in the app is Vesoldo, 43 km out in Hardanger, so a city of 290 000 people has nothing inside an hour's drive.

sources.friflyt: https://www.friflyt.no/topptur/skiturer-bergen — a per-area index in the same shape the Hemsedal round was built on: toppunkt, høydemeter, startsted, OPP/NED. It lists three tours.
sources.utno: Individual turforslag. Only the ones whose activity type is skitur are usable; the Kvamskogen hits for Såta and Fotasperrnuten are fottur, with a summer season, and describing a summer path as a ski route is the thing this pipeline exists not to do.

candidates.name: Gullfjellstoppen

published.start: Osavatnet (305 moh) i enden av vegen i Bjørndalen frå rv. 580

findings: The register's «Gullfjellet» (60.37313/5.58038) is not the summit. It reads 909,56 m against a published 987, and the highest ground within 700 m of it is 924,83. Gullfjellstoppen is 1,7 km north-north-east, at 60.38756/5.59037, where the raster reads 987,37 and the point API 986,8 — the published figure exactly. Anything that pins this tour to the register point would put the summit 62 m too low and 1,7 km from where it is.
Both intermediate heights Fri Flyt states reproduce: Osavatnet 307,0 against «305 moh», Redningshytta 597,49 against «600 moh».
The trailhead point resolves onto the lake itself (terreng Innsjø). The corridor needs a point on land at the road end before this can be routed.

candidates.name: Såta

published.start: Den innerste parkeringsplassen ved Eikedalen Skisenter på Kvamskogen

findings: The summit resolves to 1260,45 m against a published 1260 — exact.
The register carries «Iendefjell» at the same coordinate as «Såta», which corroborates Fri Flyt's «Såta, som mange kaller Iendafjellet» rather than leaving it as a claim about local usage.
Gain reproduces: 1260,45 − 456,05 = 804 m against a published 800.
Not to be confused with ut.no's Såta on Kvamskogen, which is a 404 m fottur from Mødalsvegen with a year-round season. Different start, different route, and not a ski description.
Rosselandsbotnen resolves onto water. The corridor needs a point on the shore.

candidates.name: Skrott

published.start: Støls-/hyttetunet i Fitjadalen, omtrent åtte kilometer frå Øystese

findings: Summit resolves to 1320,17 m against a published 1320 — exact.
Gain reproduces: 1320,17 − 272,38 = 1048 m against a published 1050.

The route description was only partially retrieved. The ascent via Håsete and a ski hut at about 1000 m is in hand; the descent variants are not, and the corridor should not be drawn from a half-read source.

candidates.name: Tveitakvitingen
candidates.source: ut.no/turforslag/1112154404 — «Skitur til Tveitakvitingen 1299 moh», svært krevende skitur, jan–apr, 9,0 km, 989 høydemeter
findings: Summit resolves to 1298,9 m against a published 1299 — exact.

Held rather than queued for two reasons. The route starts at Furudalen Alpinsenter and follows «preparerte løyper til Mødal»; that has to be checked against terrain class point by point along the line before anything is drawn, the way Trysilfjellet was, because a topptur line that runs in a piste sends a paying reader uphill into ski traffic. And the trailhead did not resolve — the register has no Furudalen on Kvamskogen, only Furedalen, and which of them the source means is not settled.
It also crosses the same massif as Såta — «opp mot Såta i bratte klyv og videre opp Stoveveggen» — so the two tours share ground and should be researched together.
